note: Physically he is at the far end of the ICP and commercially he is outside it. Not deconditioned is met emphatically — 33, six feet, 180 lb at roughly 16% body fat on a DEXA, multiple 100-mile races, 50 to 100 cycling miles a week, and two volcanoes climbed and skied a month before the call. Good-to-great is met precisely and in his own words: he has no physique goals, likes how he looks at 175, and wants consolidation and progression rather than transformation. On neglected_health he passes the severity test the criterion applies, since there is no crisis, though as with other calls in this batch the label reads oddly — health is the organising activity of his week, not the neglected corner of it, with the genuine exception of sleep, which he neglects deliberately and knowingly. He fails the two commercial criteria. Occupation is a sales role at a healthcare startup, which is not 'they own their own business, or they're a physician, something along those lines'; he is an employee, 33, with a first child four months away and a house move in between. On income the evidence is unambiguous and self-reported: a ceiling of $250 a month, a refusal to spend 'five times the amount that I was originally thinking of', and a stated intent to go and compare against a $199-a-month app. Two things this adds to the standing findings. First, it is the clearest case yet of the pattern the manager described internally the same day — prospects who are already athletic, already consistent and budget-anchored 'are usually the guys we send to Primal U' — which means the organisation already knows the ICP boundary and this call crossed it without anyone applying the rule; the prospect even asked for the cheaper product by name-in-substance and was told it did not exist. Second, this call and the Andrew Kline call together sharpen the existing observation in icp.json about the stated ICP having no clinical criterion: here the criterion that should have governed the conversation is bilateral recurrent shoulder instability against a programme built on overhead work, and there is no criterion in the stated ICP for that to fail either.
